title: Foreign rivalries risk turning Somalia’s political crisis into a protracted war
gist: Chatham House argues Somalia's term-extension crisis is being turned into a proxy contest between Turkey and the UAE inside a wider Red Sea bloc rivalry, raising the risk of an entrenched war and a security vacuum al-Shabaab can exploit.

insights.claim: Somalia has been in a political crisis since May 2026, when President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term was due to expire, after parliament extended terms to five years in March and the opposition rejected both that and the electoral commission's plan for April-May 2027 polls.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: No electoral timetable means continued instability around a key Red Sea chokepoint.

insights.claim: Fighting around Baidoa reportedly involved thousands of fighters plus drones and fighter jets, a more sophisticated escalation than the 2021 constitutional clashes, and the stakes are higher because the federal balance of power is in dispute.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Drone proliferation among sub-state actors raises the conflict ceiling.

insights.claim: Regional alignments have formed into two loose blocs: Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkey aligned with Sudan's army and Eritrea, versus the UAE and Israel aligned with Ethiopia.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Horn of Africa conflicts now map onto Gulf and Turkish rivalries; port and basing deals are the transmission channel.
insights.locator: The conflict in Somalia is also taking place

insights.claim: Turkey backs the federal government, with Turkish fighters reportedly involved near Baidoa (unconfirmed by Ankara), while the UAE keeps ties with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubaland and holds significant port-operation interests.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: UAE port assets in northern Somalia are exposed to the dispute; Turkish defence ties deepen.

insights.claim: In January 2026 Somalia annulled all defence and security agreements with the UAE and signed deals with Saudi Arabia and Qatar, coinciding with the Saudi-Emirati rift in Yemen.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Signals Saudi-UAE fragmentation spilling into East Africa.

insights.claim: The Houthis' advance in Yemen has reinforced the strategic value of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, boosting Somali actors' leverage, and the Houthis reportedly have growing links with al-Shabaab.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Red Sea shipping risk has a Somali land-based leg; relevant for freight and insurance.

insights.claim: Domestic elites are offering ports, corridors, economic partnerships and bases to foreign powers in exchange for backing, which fuels a feedback loop of external patronage and entrenched division.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect basing and port concessions as bargaining chips.

insights.claim: Political crises reduce security operations against al-Shabaab and ISIS-Somalia, letting them regroup, and the author calls for de-escalation via the African Union and IGAD with an interim governance agreement and a realistic election timetable.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Terror-group resurgence is the likely cost of prolonged infighting.
